days.summary: Today brings a reorganized left navigation, unrated tournaments, a redesigned offline match tool, opening a panel's console from 5stack.gg, and many fixes.

new.text: The FAQ's Playing Here section lists every in-game chat command players can use, from ready and pause to surrender and votes, with who can use each one. Searches like "unpause" or "ready up" find it.

Organizers can make a tournament unrated with an Enable ELO switch on Create and in Manage › Match Settings, until its first match starts. Unrated tournaments show an Unrated chip in the header, and their matches still count for brackets, Career XP, leaderboards, season stats and the tournament MVP.
The player page's tab row ends in a one-click 5Stack/External toggle and a Filters menu with the other match filters on every tab. A smaller version sits beside the Matches list.

Players and admins can see a player's Stacks balance and history in a side panel, and admins can give or take Stacks. Career settings now chart XP and Stacks over time, and the 5stack.gg tag payout can be configured.
Report Player asks which map a report is about when more than one map was played, and only offers rounds that were played on that map. Moderators see the map and round on the case.

The offline match tool is redesigned to match 5stack.gg. Matches sit in a sidebar with a docked RCON console, and the create form is laid out like the Create Match page, with map tiles and a starting side per map. Options are readable, the tool uses its own confirm dialogs, and it no longer loads anything from the internet.
Offline match pages have a status bar with Force Ready, Skip Knife, Pause or Resume. A Fix a Problem menu can rewind a round, restart the map, kick a player or restart an unresponsive game server.
Offline matches keep their progress through a game server restart, restore rounds locally, and end the map and series on a surrender. Editing a match keeps the series unless its maps or teams change.
The offline match tool has its own sign-in page with a random password per node. Admins copy it from the node inspector's Offline section or read it on the node, and the guides explain both.

The node inspector shows whether a node is ready for offline matches. Nodes keep the panel's game server image downloaded and refresh it hourly while online, and the offline tool can pull an image when one is missing.
Administrators can set a logo for a public server, shown beside its name on the Public Servers cards.
A node with a graphics card 5Stack isn't using shows an "Unused graphics card" hardware warning that admins can acknowledge for everyone. The node warnings guide lists it.

Setup can manage your panel's Cloudflare zone with one scoped API token, setting up DNS records, the proxy and HTTPS for you. Records you made yourself are only replaced after you agree, and this works for new installs and existing panels.

You can open your panel's console from My Settings → Panels on 5stack.gg, where pressing Open Console approves it and opens it in its own window. The Browser Console guide and a new Console People guide cover this, along with the Admin and Read only roles and downloading recovery backups.

Administrators get a notification when their Cloudflare storage worker is out of date, and another once it's updated. It is checked shortly after the panel starts and every 15 minutes. The demo settings also flag an outdated worker and say to update the panel, then run the Cloudflare setup again.
Shortly after the panel starts, it sends a small test demo through storage and notifies administrators if demo uploads are failing, and again once they work.
The left navigation is reorganized:
A Steam group button sits next to every Discord button and opens the FAQ's clan-tag guide.

improved.text: The tournament header has an "Organized by" line, with linked organizer teams first, then the organizers.
The player page's Community tab opens on one summary card with points and server ranks, time played and last seen. Stats a server hasn't reported are no longer shown as zero.
Career XP is now the same for everyone in a match: 160 XP per match plus 80 for a win, with 1,000 XP and 2,500 Stacks per level. XP by rating is gone, and existing progress is recounted.
Operator alerts now push to administrators by default, while job results stay off unless turned on. Administrators who had turned infrastructure pushes off keep them off.

Adding a game server node asks for the whole code the node prints, one box per character, and a paste fills them all. The approve step can also set the CPU governor to performance and turn on full kernel preemption before the node joins, using switch rows like the settings page.

An offline match's server password is now called the Admin password, since only admins and casters need it to join as spectators. It is random for each new match and shown on the match page with a Copy button, and editing a match no longer changes it.
The offline match tool, its RCON console and each node's file and plugin access are better protected, and each offline match has its own RCON password.

The Cloudflare storage worker and media uploads are hardened, and unfinished uploads are cleared from storage after a day. To get the new worker, update the panel, then run the Cloudflare setup again.
The System Update list names services in plain words, such as API, Web app, Demo parser, Rokkan and Game node connector.

The install guides follow today's setup page, including managed Cloudflare and the reverse proxy step. They are shorter and focus on what to run, click and decide, and the architecture diagram has its own How It Fits Together page.
The Run your own page plays the install video, with speed controls, theater mode and full screen, and the install guide uses the same player. A new diagram shows how game server nodes join.
News, comments, moderation lists, awards, the cosmetic picker, the utility book and other lists load more as you scroll instead of needing a Show more button.
On phones, menus open as bottom sheets, tabs lay out in even rows, the hub opens without a stutter, and tap targets are bigger. Highlights also show one clip per screen.
Apps such as Inventory show their own page names in the breadcrumbs instead of their web address.
Signing in with Steam is better protected, and a sign-in must be finished within five minutes.
The FAQ and the browser tab title use the "Find your five" tagline.

fixed.text: A Rush tournament's brackets, stage tabs and stage settings show Bo1 even when a stage was set up as Bo3 before the switch to Rush.
The render queue shows when a highlight finished and how long the rendered clip is.
Only a clip's owner can change its title.
The player header no longer leaves a gap above Career after the ELO chart grows.
Draft lobbies, lineups, party seats and the friends list show the colorway a player picked for their frame and nameplate.
Changing an award's rewards no longer tells players who received the award right afterward that it now unlocks rewards they already have.
A player who isn't allowed on a server is turned away once instead of retrying forever and taking up a slot.
An offline public server no longer makes a region with healthy nodes show as Partial.
Nodes pinned to a game server image from a registry with a port pull the right image again.
Offline matches are more reliable:

In the node inspector, the LAN IP link opens the offline match tool, and an acknowledged warning shows who acknowledged it on one line. A node's clock going backward no longer extends an offline tool sign-in lockout.
Demo uploads work again on panels whose storage address points at their own built-in storage.
A demo, clip or video requested before its upload finished no longer stays missing in the browser for a month.
Open Console no longer asks players already signed in to 5stack.gg to sign in with Steam again.
An unpinned hub closes again once the pointer leaves it.
The 5Stack wordmark, the new tab icon and other recently added images load again for browsers that had kept a broken copy.

days.summary: 5Stack gets a new look, seasons gain their own awards, tournaments can seed teams by ELO, and the Steam presence bot is easier to add and keep online.

new.text: Typing .stop in game starts a vote to replay the round being played, including the first round, with no round number needed.

Organizers choose By ELO or Random seeding, and By ELO is the default for new tournaments. Before registration closes, the Teams tab shows each team's seeding ELO, its projected seed and its round-one opponent.
A team's seed stays visible for the whole tournament, in the bracket, the Swiss and round-robin standings, and on the match page. Hovering a seed in the bracket traces that team's route.

Awards can give Locker items and Stacks. Organizers set these on the tournament Prize Board. Players see what they can win before play, on the finished podium, in the award popup, in a Locker Awards tab and in Stacks History.
The Prize Board can pay Stacks and items to 1st through 3rd even with a tournament's awards turned off, and placing players get a notice when they win.

Seasons have their own awards. Admins set awards and Stacks for 1st, 2nd, 3rd and MVP on a podium, add stat awards, and choose what carries over to the next season. The leaderboard shows the current leaders and prizes.
Every panel gets nine built-in stat awards and default Stacks prizes for its first season, so seasons hand out awards without any setup.
A Player Backgrounds switch in My Account hides the backgrounds other players wear on their profiles.
Players' looks appear on one shared player card on Play seats, the leaderboard top 3 and events. Frames and nameplates also show in the friends list, party seats, voice tiles and notifications.

Admins get a bell alert when the Steam presence bot goes offline or needs a Steam Guard code, and can enter the code right from the notification. Players see a notice on their card while the bot is offline.
Administrators can keep a dedicated Ranked server to ranked or tournament matches, so it loads the right plugins for them. The match server picker greys out servers kept to another kind of match.
Two new check scripts verify a GPU node or a Proxmox LXC container. They come with a guide for setting up a dedicated machine, a VM or a Proxmox LXC container for NVIDIA or AMD.
The docs add a Managing Nodes guide and cover the admin settings for GPU workloads and video encoding.

5Stack has a new look. The welcome page leads with "Find your five.", and the site, icons, in-game messages and Discord posts use the new mark and wordmark. Sites with a custom logo or name keep theirs.
News articles post to their own Discord channel when first published. Admins set the webhook and optional role mentions in Settings → News.
The docs add guides for Career and the Locker, Rokkan, Inventory and Sticker Crafts, Getting Around, and moderation.

improved.text: Lineups you save on your practice server land in a This Server group at the top of Mine, numbered on the map in the order you saved them. The Public tab shows only public lineups again.
The 3D replay keeps crates, cars and lamps that were missing and colours props as props. It also removes stray backdrop buildings and rooftop antennas and smooths the shadows under props.
The outro at the end of every highlight clip is rebuilt around the new 5Stack mark and ends on "Find your five".
My Account accepts an avatar URL again, next to the upload option.

Career is on by default and open to every player, and admins can still turn it off or raise the minimum role. On panels that had it off, players receive everything they unlocked with their next match.
Adding the Steam presence bot now uses a one-use Steam invite link, so players become friends at once without friend-request errors or waiting.
Reading and deleting notifications takes effect immediately, and deletes can be undone for 5 seconds. Tap targets are larger on touch devices.
Notification cards open from anywhere you click, and new-article notifications show the cover beside the title.
The CS2 build card shows Gamedata and Map assets as separate tiles, each opening its own panel, and fits better on phones.
Past times an hour or more old show the exact time across the site, including notifications.
The changelog's new-entries dot follows your account, so reading it on one device clears it everywhere.
Signing in from the welcome page takes you to your player page.
Webhook URLs, API keys and passwords in settings are hidden by default, with an eye button to reveal them.

fixed.text: The Coach page no longer scrolls sideways on phones. Match rows there and on player pages show a shorter date.
A demo playback no longer stops when the viewer's connection drops or reconnects.
The reparse-all-demos warning now says demos are reparsed two at a time.
Streams from AMD nodes no longer drop large keyframes, so they stop skipping frames.
1440p streams are no longer cropped to part of the picture, and demo streams lag less. Demo streams now go out at 1440p when rendered at 1440p.
A season whose end date simply passes now hands out its awards.
Admins can move a season's end date past the start of the next scheduled season, and that season now moves with it. Make ongoing, End now and editing the next scheduled season also work as expected.
The Steam presence bot recovers on its own from failed logins and accepts friend requests sent while it was offline. It also frees a player's connection when they unfriend it.
Matches with a custom game mode now play only on on-demand servers, so the mode's plugins load. The server picker explains why dedicated servers are unavailable for these matches.
Fresh installs on k3s 1.37 no longer fail while k3s is still setting up the Gateway API.
On panels not behind Cloudflare, rate limits count each visitor separately instead of sharing one limit across everyone.
The 5Stack logo no longer shows as a broken image for people who loaded the site during an update.
The welcome page no longer shows an error while scrolling.
The default language picker shows a space between the flag and the language name.

days.summary: A large day: community polls, a reworked coach review and Utility map, Stacks rewards for awards and the 5stack.gg tag, confirmations before tournament teardowns, and new health warnings for game server nodes.

new.text: Each mode tile on the Play page has an info icon that shows the mode's current map pool when you hover or tap it, without selecting the mode. Premier and FACEIT show the Competitive pool.
Organizers and staff can reset a captains' draft back to its first pick from the draft room's admin dock, after a confirm. Captains and players are kept, and the pick clock restarts.
Players placed into a tournament's medals or MVP get one notification when the tournament finishes.

The Utility tab's throw map shows each side of the match on its own map, or one map with a CT / T toggle on narrow screens. It adds zoom, panning and a legend, and clicking a throw focuses on it with Watch and See the Meta Spot.
Bots standing when you save a lineup are saved with it, and the drop key stands them back up. Dropping weapons is turned off on practice servers to make room for this.
The utility map shows a lineup's bots with their own icon, and lineups with bots carry a badge.
Players left idle on a practice server get two warnings and are then kicked. Admins set the time under Settings › Application › Utility; it is 15 minutes by default, and 0 turns it off.
The coach review shows the player's K/A/D, ADR, KAST, HLTV rating and lineup accuracy. It also has tabs for Overview, Worked, To fix and Utility, which together show everything Rokkan wrote.
The Awards leaderboard has a Special column and a fourth podium dot, so players with only Special awards now appear on it.
Teams can set a country in their settings, shown as a flag beside the team name on the team page, in the match header and in tournament team lists.
A name change request asks the player why, and staff can reply with a comment the player receives. A player can only have one request open at a time.

Awards can give Locker items and Stacks to every holder. Tournament organizers can also set rewards per placement, and admins per season placement. Adding a reward pays existing holders and tells them.
40 looks for your profile stat print the number straight on your banner, and the stat now shows on your player page too. The Locker shows the 250 Stacks it costs to clear a pinned stat.

Wearing the 5stack.gg clan tag in imported Steam or FACEIT matches pays 100 Stacks per match, plus a one-time 2,000 bonus. The Support card and FAQ explain it, and the thank-you notifications stack in the bell.
Nodes warn when CS2, the game streamer or k3s keep their files on a spinning hard drive.
Nodes warn when their CPU is split across too many sockets, and advise setting the VM to one socket.
GPU nodes warn when Secure Boot or something else keeps the NVIDIA driver from loading, or when kernel modesetting is off. A node whose NVIDIA driver didn't load still shows in the panel.
Administrators can acknowledge a node warning so it stops being flagged. Acknowledged warnings stay listed under Hardware with Restore, and a changed warning is flagged again.
The in-game scoreboard's Server Website button opens 5stack.gg on servers running the SwiftlyS2 version of the plugin.
When both a 5Stack service update and a panel release are available, the update center offers a single Update that runs them in order. Opening the update center also checks for updates.
A Storage guide explains which paths need an SSD or NVMe disk and how to move game files onto one.
The changelog groups each day by section of 5Stack and tags each change New, Improved or Fixed. Wide screens also get a Sections list for showing just one section.
Match organizers and above see a dot on the profile menu when the changelog has new days.
Community polls appear at the top of News, and the bell tells you when one opens. Any signed-in player can vote once and sees results as the poll allows, and anyone who can post news can run polls.
Upload, crop, replace or remove your avatar under Settings → My Account. Removing it goes back to your Steam avatar.
Click a GIF in chat to see it larger.

improved.text: Check-in now appears in the match header's VS box instead of a card on the Overview, with the same camera gate and red last ten seconds as the draft room. On phones, the teams stack beside it.
Call for Support in the match menu now asks before paging the organizers.
Deleting a map shows which pools it leaves. A matchmaking pool's last map can no longer be deleted or removed from the pool.
Opening a finished match no longer rolls in every number at once. Stats show their value straight away and only animate when they change.
With several tournaments live, the Tournaments page gives each one an equal tab above the live feature.

The Teams tab shows a card grid in seed order with Expand all and Collapse all, and your own team shows full width with its roster open. The check-in panel now shows how many teams have checked in instead of listing them all.

Deleting, cancelling or resetting a tournament now asks first. If matches have been played, it lists the ones that would be deleted along with their demos and clips, and you must tick a box to confirm. Matches still in progress block it until they end.
Leave pool on the Free Agents tab asks first and explains what leaving costs you.
The event overview shows every match in play or getting ready, plus a tab for each live tournament with its full bracket. The header's Watch live opens a match that is actually being played.
Deleting a league season or resetting it to setup lists the played matches it would delete and needs them confirmed.
In theater mode, the review's side column grows wider when there's room, so tabs and utility rows no longer get cut off.
The top bar shows the path to the open review, scouting report or habits page.
Rokkan can now tell one lineup thrown twice apart from two different lineups.
A demo replay in a tab that stays hidden for 5 minutes stops and offers Watch again. A page opened in the background doesn't start a replay until you look at it.
The stream address now only serves playback and snapshots.
Stats table headers are quieter. Only the sorted column shows an arrow, and a Stats Guide button sits beside the controls.
The top-bar profile menu opens on a mini version of your profile card. It shows your banner, frame, level, title, flag, ELO and pinned stat.
The new-tournament notification shows the tournament's banner, name and start time in your own time zone, and the push says when it starts.
Looking at any 5Stack tab clears the flashing title and badge in all your other 5Stack tabs.

Staff can see removed sanctions and abandons, dimmed, with who removed them and when. Match organizers can see each abandon's ladder step and cooldown, and a removed abandon no longer counts against the player.
A banned player's notice says how long the ban lasts, or that it is permanent.
Traefik now binds the host's ports itself, so the panel sees players' real addresses when k3s runs on a VPN or private node address.

The update popover shows an update starting as soon as you press Update. After a minute without progress, it says so and offers Try Again. Updates now finish as soon as the run ends, and new matches resume right away.
A panel that uses external storage no longer runs the built-in storage service.

The NVIDIA GPU guide adds a step to turn on kernel modesetting, which clip capture needs. The AMD guide covers a kernel option that stops the driver from loading, and notes that a bad memory setting now stops the panel at startup, with the log naming the problem.
Past times an hour or more old show the exact time instead of "3 days ago". Presence, live ages and countdowns still count.
Chat videos recorded by OBS, ShadowPlay or phones are optimized after upload, so they start and seek faster.
Player and match pages draw each section once in its final place, so nothing jumps around while they load.

Dropdowns are lighter, especially on tournament stage forms. The friends list, matchmaking and the Play page's live queue count do less work, and players going offline no longer slows the rest of the site.
The browser extension's FACEIT import, when it needs to, opens the match room in a background tab and closes it when done.

fixed.text: The scoreboard's HLTV column shows the rating again.
Lineup names stay on every player's in-game scoreboard for the whole match, not only the first seconds after going live.
Restoring a round no longer records false stats or loses a real round. A restarted server can no longer play over rounds that were already recorded.
A map's label is kept when maps are refreshed, and editing it updates the map in every mode.
Free agent sign-up times show the day once a sign-up is from an earlier day.
Rebuilding a cancelled tournament keeps leftover matches that still have demos or clips. Deleting a stage that has matches no longer fails.
The throw map's hints make sense on touch screens, and zooming while dragging no longer resets when you let go.
The flash card counts a player as blinded for 1s+ based on the seconds it shows, so a 3.0s flash no longer reads "0 of 1".
A lineup you save in a practice server now shows on the Public tab and the map while you are in that server.
Practice saves that couldn't reach 5Stack are retried automatically and are never saved twice. A refused save now tells you instead of blocking later saves.
Watch in the coach review no longer gets stuck after jumping past a throw. Phrases like "R8 bomb 0:31" now read as a round, not the Revolver.
Closing the demo viewer while a clip is rendering no longer stops you from making new clips.
The 2D and 3D replay buttons only appear once the map is confirmed to have a replay.
When a live stream switches matches, the HUD no longer shows the new match's teams over the old match's end screen.
Highlight renders take a free GPU in the order they were queued, and a freed GPU is picked up sooner.
On NVIDIA nodes, streams and highlights always render on the NVIDIA GPU instead of another device on the node.
Damage with the M4A1-S, USP-S, CZ75-Auto, R8 Revolver and MP5-SD is now recorded under the right gun. Older matches are corrected where possible, so Arsenal no longer shows 0 ADR for them.
On profiles with a background, tabs, cards, tables and empty states sit on frosted glass, so the background no longer runs through the text.
The player page's All / 5Stack / External filter bar no longer wraps.
Avatar frames look the same on the profile card as on their Locker tile.
The Locker's tabs show as icons, with the selected tab named and hover names on the rest, so all seven fit on any screen.
Award notifications open the award they are for.
File manager uploads of up to 100 MB now work on panels behind Cloudflare's proxy.
The dedicated servers list shows the plugin version for community servers.
Enabling, disabling or restarting a dedicated server in quick succession no longer leaves it in the wrong state.
Fresh installs on k3s 1.37 or later no longer fail, because the Gateway API resources are left to k3s.
Long steps in the header update popover wrap instead of being cut off.
Deleting demos and clips now removes their files from versioned storage buckets. If a file can't be removed, its demo or clip is kept so the delete can be retried.
When Detect can't reach a plugin, the settings page says why instead of "Failed to fetch".
Links to 5Stack show their previews in Discord, Slack and Steam again, and search engines see the welcome page instead of an error.
My Account no longer blocks saving your country and language with "Invalid input".
Signing in, signing out or switching accounts in one tab now updates your other open tabs, chat included.
When your role changes, the open page adjusts to it without a reload.
Country flags show properly on Windows in all text styles.

days.summary: Today brings community leaderboards with far more stats, profile backgrounds in the Locker, a reworked Utility tab and many fixes across practice, tournaments and notifications.

new.text: A match's Utility tab draws every throw on a radar against the meta lineups that three or more players throw. Throws on the spot are solid, and missed throws are dashed with a ring at the meta spot. Each player shows their meta throws on the spot, and Watch opens the 2D replay at the throw.
Rokkan knows when each team could hear an enemy running or shooting, so reviews stop treating every enemy position as something players knew.
Rokkan's reviews compare utility against meta lineups and count the same throws the Utility tab shows. A utility moment is marked "Round N · utility", and the replay rings where the meta throw lands.

Clip actions are the same icons everywhere, with Share opening Copy link and Download. A clip's owner and staff get Public and Delete buttons, and a deleted clip leaves every list and playlist without a reload.
The Public Servers page shows one leaderboard across every public server you can open. Game mode chips narrow the weekly board.

Community leaderboards rank by many more stats, including K/D, HS %, assists, MVPs, points, accuracy, best streak, trades, utility, kill types and objectives. They also add weapon boards and community seasons. Click a column header to rank by it, and values below a column's minimum are dimmed.

A profile's Community tab gets a game mode filter, K/D, HS %, assists and MVP tiles, and Modes and Maps tables. Servers running the updated plugin also show points, accuracy, best streak, utility, hitgroups, kill types, objectives and a per weapon table.
Profile backgrounds: 100 scenes to wear behind your whole profile, with cards turning to frosted glass. The Locker has a Backgrounds tab, and Grant Reward can give them.
The Locker shows the background you are trying or wearing across the whole Career page, and each worn item can be taken off for free.
Read notifications stay in place and dim instead of moving, and the bulk actions become one button in the panel heading: Dismiss All, then Delete Dismissed.
One click on an unread notification's dot marks it read, and one click on a read notification's dot deletes it, with an animated dot.
Supporters get a thank-you notification the first time a demo shows them wearing the 5stack.gg tag, and the Support 5Stack card steps aside once the tag is seen.

The node inspector fixes the CPU governor and legacy lowlatency kernel warnings in one click and can turn low latency on or off. It asks before any change that needs a reboot, and never reboots the node itself.
A game node that cannot reach its panel shows why in the update center and the node inspector. Removing a node tells you when its Tailscale device was left behind.
With the update policy on Manual, the 5Stack service no longer updates itself. The update center shows it as ready, and it installs only when an admin presses Update Now.
The update center points out a graphics card on a game node that is not being used and links to the GPU node guide.

improved.text: The Play page's waiting count and queue updates stay quick as queues fill, and reconnecting no longer reloads every queued lobby.
The 2K to 5K tiles in the lineup overview's multi-kills popover are underlined when they open a round breakdown.
Community stats remember which map and game mode each session was played on, and keep a daily history after older sessions are cleared.
Leaderboards show fades and buttons on edges with more columns to scroll to.
Hovering a Career tile or background no longer changes your card or the page; a click previews it.
Moving backgrounds stay smooth on profiles and in the Locker, and the heaviest animated scenes draw much faster.
The one-time "Career levels are here" banner is gone.
On community servers, the CS2 server plugin reports assists, headshots, damage, rounds, MVPs, detailed counters and per weapon totals, plus each map's final counts. Nothing played in warmup counts.
Approving a node join checks the fingerprint the node printed on its screen.
The welcome page's "Watch live" button now reads "Open app".

fixed.text: When a matchmaking queue is turned off, lobbies can no longer end up back in it waiting for a match that never comes. Affected players get a message saying why.
Add New Map shows its Name field again, Workshop maps save without pressing Refresh, an existing map is not added twice, and a failed Steam lookup shows an error.
Stats from the round in progress when a restore starts no longer count twice. That round's late score also no longer removes rounds a restore can still return to.
Deleted maps no longer appear in the practice and utility map pickers, and matches played on them still show the map.
Setting a match winner, taking back veto picks, changing a match's maps and deleting a match now always go through the panel's own checks.
Tournament cards, Quick Look and the next-up strip no longer offer Register on invite-only tournaments or to people already in, and show a joined chip instead.
Free-agent-only tournaments offer "Join as a free agent" instead of "Register a team" on their cards.
Revoke no longer shows on calculated tournament awards, and season grants keep it.
Removing a category from a tournament works again.
On a map split across two demos, Save and Watch on the Utility tab use the demo the throw came from.
A practice save thrown on a different map from the session's is refused instead of being filed under the wrong map. Practice servers on the wrong map are moved to the booked map.
A practice save or result that is sent again no longer creates a duplicate lineup or counts twice towards streaks and mastery. A save or score sent at a busy moment is retried instead of lost.
The practice HUD comes back after a player reconnects.
Player paths no longer show someone moving between callouts while they stood near a callout boundary. An admin's review of an older match re-reads its demo to pick this up.
Apply Look really buys, charges for and equips your changes, and the profile shows the picked colorway and roll.
The Match Rewards panel appears on finished matches again.
Cosmetics show to everyone, including signed-out visitors, while the Career setting still controls Stacks and the Career page.
Founder, Legend and other items no longer show twice, and the Grant Reward picker only lists available items.
Admins can give themselves rewards with Grant Reward.
Match rows and Locker panels sit on frosted glass over a background, long names fit the profile card, and a nameplate lines up with the rank under it.
A stack marked read keeps its green check for a moment after it moves, so the next click no longer deletes it by accident.
The update center shows settings changes and script runs as what they are, and a setup run from the terminal never shows as a failed panel update.
An invalid AMD GPU memory setting for streams now stops the panel at startup and shows the rejected values, instead of failing when a stream or render starts.
Pages in Safari load again on refresh.
Match logs, system logs and RCON command suggestions show player names and plugin text as plain text.

days.summary: Career levels and the Locker arrive, stats count team kills and suicides the same way everywhere, and self-hosted panels get clearer update controls and easier node removal.

new.text: Career levels arrive, with frames, level badges and nameplates on player rows and profile cards, a Career page with your track, the Locker and Stacks, match rewards and a one-time welcome banner. Applying a look in the Locker buys and wears it on your account, and banners and frames come with a pattern you can reroll for Stacks.

On agent-managed panels, removing a node can also uninstall 5Stack from its server, and this option is on by default. The dialog keeps showing progress after a reload and offers Remove Anyway if the uninstall fails.
Managed panels have a Settings > Panel updates page for choosing when updates install. The header now shows the panel only when an update is waiting on you.

Managed panels that keep secrets in an external secret store now warn in the header when secrets can't sync, with a settings page that lists each failing secret, why it fails and how to fix it. Check Now asks for a resync, and an update that is missing secrets lists them before it starts.

When a panel update rolls back, admins get a notification with the reason and the header shows it in amber. Automatic and scheduled updates skip a release that failed on your panel, and you can still install it with Update Now.
Existing panels installed from a git checkout can move onto the 5Stack service and keep their configuration and secrets.

improved.text: Coach reviews, scouting reports and habits now have their own page addresses, and older review and scouting links still open the right page.
Player search shows Played with recently above Friends, and you can fold the section shut. It stays folded in that browser.
Pending team, tournament and draft invites in the bell now show as cards with Deny and Accept under the headline, and a plain team invite names who invited you and to which team.
Adding a node with a join code looks the code up as soon as the sixth digit is entered, so there is no Find button to press.
The slow CPU governor warning gives the command to fix it, with a copy button, and links to the CPU Governance docs. Nodes whose governor can't be read no longer show the warning.
The header's panel row now reads as one line, such as "Panel 2026.11.1.2 is ready".

New matches are held during a panel update only when the update needs it, and matches already running carry on. Your own node on/off settings are no longer changed, and held matches start once the update finishes.
The nightly database backup checks that the storage bucket belongs to your S3 account before uploading, and the backup job shows as failed if it doesn't.
Several pages put less load on the site while open and stay faster under heavy traffic: match page highlight clips, player profiles, the Play page and public server lists, and the Scrim Finder board.

fixed.text: Opening a review, scouting report or habits on the coach page now adds a browser history step, so Back returns to the list. The list's tab, map and player filters survive a reload.

Team kills and suicides no longer count as kills, and assists on a teammate's death no longer count as assists, and stored lifetime and season totals have been corrected. Tournament and event stats tabs now match the tournament leaderboard, and ELO and stage tiebreakers use the same rule from the next match on.
Played with recently in player search now lists the players you recently played with instead of staying empty.
In slim notification rows, wrapped lines now start at the row's edge, and a paused match row is the same height as other rows.
The award notification now leads with the award's name and shows its badge on the right, so the badge no longer covers the title.
A node added with a join code now starts enabled and takes matches right away.
A node removed from its own server with the 5Stack command line now also disappears from the panel.
On panels installed by the 5Stack service, game server nodes are no longer shown as unsupported when node networking is already set up.
Panels with played matches can update again, and the leaderboard no longer fails after an update.
The setup scripts' node prompt only accepts a number from its list and asks again otherwise.
